neighbours.label: ' up' after 'stand' / 'stood' / 'standing', in the literal and the 'stand up to' sense
fire: Sooner or later you must stand up to your older brother.
The old man stood up slowly and walked to the door.
The doctor recommends standing up every hour during long flights.
All the students stood up when the headmaster came in.
She has the courage to stand up for her beliefs at work.
The dog stands up on its back legs when it hears the bag.
It takes real nerve to stand up in court and say that.
He stood up to the mayor and demanded an answer.
quiet: Sooner or later you must pick up your older brother.
The old man looked up slowly and walked to the door.
The doctor recommends standing still every hour during long flights.
All the students cheered up when the headmaster came in.
She has the courage to stand by her beliefs at work.
The dog sits down on its back legs when it hears the bag.
It takes real nerve to show up in court and say that.
He wrote up the mayor and demanded an answer.

notes: Card: ' up' x30 of the top 32, nearly all after stand/stood. Probe: 'stand up to a bully' 0.710; 'stood up' 0.813; 'Standing up' 0.676; 'woke up' 0.272; 'picked up' and 'went up' below 0.015; 'stand by' 0.016. Near misses keep ' up' after other verbs, or 'stand' with another particle.
